meta.title: The City People Think Is Made Up -- But Isn't
meta._convention: One scene-spec JSON per script, saved alongside it as <script-name>.scenes.json. Each beat's `duration` is intentionally omitted -- build_video.js fills it in at render time from the ACTUAL measured length of that beat's generated narration WAV.
meta._note: Mali is a real country polygon (highlight: ["ML"]). Timbuktu itself is a marker since individual cities aren't resolved as polygons; the Niger River bend near Timbuktu and old caravan/rescue routes are drawn via `lines`.

beats.voText: People use this city's name as a joke for the middle of nowhere. It's real, and it used to be one of the richest cities on Earth.
beats.onScreenText: It's real. And it was rich.

beats.voText: It's Timbuktu, in modern-day Mali, sitting near the Niger River on the southern edge of the Sahara Desert.
beats.onScreenText: Timbuktu, Mali. On the Sahara's edge.

beats.voText: For centuries it was a major center of the gold and salt trade, funneling caravan wealth across the desert and into the wider world.
beats.onScreenText: A capital of gold and salt trade.

beats.voText: It was also a major center of Islamic scholarship, home to libraries holding hundreds of thousands of ancient manuscripts.
In 2012, when militants threatened to destroy them, residents secretly smuggled most of those manuscripts out of the city to save them.
A real population, a real airport, and a real history stranger than the legend. Timbuktu was never the middle of nowhere. Follow for more places on Earth that shouldn't exist, but do.
